sources.entry: Password Pusher - Dead-simple application to securely communicate passwords (or text) over the web. Passwords automatically expire after a certain number of views and/or time has passed. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/K8S/Ruby

summary.one_liner: Password Pusher is an open source web app for sharing passwords, notes, files, or URLs through self-deleting links that expire after a set number of views and/or time.
summary.what_it_does: Users push a password, note, file, or URL and receive a one-time link that expires after a view limit and/or time limit. The README says stored data is encrypted at rest and removed once expired, and links can require a passphrase. An audit log records when links were created and viewed, and by whom when logins are used. The app offers optional TOTP two-factor authentication with backup codes, and admins can require MFA instance-wide via PWP__REQUIRE_MFA=true. It includes a built-in admin dashboard, a JSON API v2 (/api/v2) plus legacy v1-style routes, and an official pwpush CLI. The UI is available in 31 languages with light and dark themes, and branding can be changed through environment variables. It can run stateless or with a database for persistence.
use_cases: share a password with a colleague via a self-deleting link
send a sensitive note that expires after one view
share files or URLs securely with an audit trail
push secrets from the terminal with the pwpush CLI
self-host a secure secret-sharing service for a team
deploy a temporary secret-sharing page on a PaaS
how_to_run: Point a DNS record to your server (e.g. pwpush.example.com)
Clone this repo or download docker-compose.yml
In docker-compose.yml, uncomment and set TLS_DOMAIN (for automatic Let's Encrypt TLS) and optionally PWPUSH_MASTER_KEY
notable: Audit logs showing who created and viewed each push
Expiry by view count and/or time, with optional passphrase
JSON API v2 plus an official CLI and Chrome extension
31 UI languages and 26 Bootswatch themes via env vars
One-click deploy options on several hosting platforms
caveats: Pro features are split from the open source edition; some features are only in the paid pwpush.com or Self-Hosted Pro offering
Donation link is temporarily disabled per the README
Full self-hosting requires a server, DNS setup, and TLS configuration
